research_profile.summary_bio: Shama Abidi (MPhil in Pharmacy Practice, Department of Pharmacy Practice, Faculty of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences, University of Karachi, Karachi, Pakistan) is a Senior Pharmacist / Clinical Pharmacist at Department of Pharmacy Services, Liaquat National Hospital and Medical College, Karachi, Pakistan. Her verified research portfolio spans 5 peer-reviewed publications and conference abstracts in the Pakistan Journal of Pharmaceutical Sciences (PJPS) and Journal of Pharmaceutical Policy and Practice (JPPP), focusing on ICU carbapenem antimicrobial stewardship (N=134, 87.3% physician acceptance), antianginal pharmacotherapy outcomes (N=110, SAQ-7 & Naranjo ADR assessment), high-alert medication safety (N=60), and AI vs. clinical pharmacist interventions.

research_documents.journal_or_venue: Journal of Pharmaceutical Policy and Practice (Abstract 223, PESP Conference 2025 Part A) (Vol. 18, No. S2, 2485639, pp. 146-147)
research_documents.extracted_text:
Title: Evaluating knowledge of high-alert medications among nurses, pharmacists, and clinicians to improve medication safety
Authors: Fatima Baig, Aqsa Bilekhia, Shama Abidi, Safia Ahmed
Journal: Journal of Pharmaceutical Policy and Practice (Abstract 223, PESP Conference 2025 Part A) (Vol. 18, No. S2, 2485639, pp. 146-147)
DOI: 10.1080/20523211.2025.2485639
Study Site: Liaquat National Hospital & Medical College, Karachi
Ethics Approval: Liaquat National Hospital and Medical College, Karachi
Sample Size: N = 60 healthcare professionals (20 clinicians, 20 nurses, 20 pharmacists) + 6-month HAM consumption audit
Key Evidence Summary: Assessed hospital staff knowledge and 6-month consumption patterns (June-Nov 2024) of High-Alert Medications (HAMs), specifically electrolytes. Pharmacists achieved the highest knowledge score (80%), followed by nurses (75%) and clinicians (70%), identifying targeted gaps in drug compatibility, storage, and labeling.

research_documents.authors_json: ["Fatima Baig", "Haris Aziz Siddiqui", "Aqsa Bilekhia", "Shama Abidi", "Safia Ahmed"]
research_documents.journal_or_venue: Journal of Pharmaceutical Policy and Practice (Abstract 225, PESP Conference 2025 Part A) (Vol. 18, No. S2, 2485639, p. 149)
research_documents.extracted_text:
Title: AI meets human expertise: Comparision between clinical pharmacist interventions and artificial intelligence at a tertiary care hospital in Pakistan
Authors: Fatima Baig, Haris Aziz Siddiqui, Aqsa Bilekhia, Shama Abidi, Safia Ahmed
Journal: Journal of Pharmaceutical Policy and Practice (Abstract 225, PESP Conference 2025 Part A) (Vol. 18, No. S2, 2485639, p. 149)
DOI: 10.1080/20523211.2025.2485639
Study Site: Liaquat National Hospital & Medical College, Karachi
Ethics Approval: Liaquat National Hospital and Medical College, Karachi
Sample Size: N = 60 patients over 6 months (June - November 2024)
Key Evidence Summary: Prospective study comparing clinical pharmacist interventions with AI (ChatGPT 4.0) across drug-drug interactions, renal-adjusted antibiotic dosing, and electrolyte imbalance management. Validated by 3 independent clinical pharmacists; demonstrated that while AI detected DDIs and electrolyte issues, human clinical pharmacists were indispensable for accurate renal-adjusted antibiotic dosing in ICU settings.

Title: Effectiveness and safety assessment of calcium channel blockers compared to beta blockers in patients with angina: An observational study
Authors: Shama Abidi (First Author), Saira Saeed Khan, Sadaf Naeem, Humera Siddiqui, Sumaira Khadim, Saima Saleem, Saira Erum Ejaz, Syed Ishtiaq Rasool, Syeda Maheen Zahidi
Journal: Pakistan Journal of Pharmaceutical Sciences (Pak. J. Pharm. Sci.) (Vol. 37, No. 3, May 2024, pp. 639-649)
DOI: 10.36721/PJPS.2024.37.3.REG.639-649.1
Study Site: Liaquat National Hospital & Medical College, Karachi
Ethics Approval: IBC KU-317/2023 (Institutional Bio-ethical Research Committee, University of Karachi)
Sample Size: N = 110 angina patients (61 male, 49 female; June 2022 - June 2023)
Key Evidence Summary: Evaluated Beta Blockers (BB, 36.36%), Calcium Channel Blockers (CCB, 54.4%), and CCB+BB combination (9.8%) in tertiary care cardiology OPDs using Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ-7) and Naranjo ADR scale. Improved angina symptoms in 83/110 patients (p < 0.05). CCB SAQ-7 score (83.97 ± 3.18) and combination (82.64 ± 5.12) outperformed BB (80.46 ± 5.99), with CCB exhibiting fewer Definite/Probable ADRs over long-term angina control.

research_documents.title: Evaluation of carbapenem antimicrobial stewardship program at a tertiary care hospital: A prospective interventional study
research_documents.authors_json: ["Fizzah Ali", "Tabassum Zehra", "Nazir Ahmed Solangi", "Karim Ullah Makki", "Haris Aziz Siddiqui", "Shama Abidi"]
research_documents.journal_or_venue: Pakistan Journal of Pharmaceutical Sciences (Pak. J. Pharm. Sci.) (Vol. 35, No. 6, November 2022, pp. 1595-1601)
research_documents.extracted_text:
Title: Evaluation of carbapenem antimicrobial stewardship program at a tertiary care hospital: A prospective interventional study
Authors: Fizzah Ali, Tabassum Zehra, Nazir Ahmed Solangi, Karim Ullah Makki, Haris Aziz Siddiqui, Shama Abidi
Journal: Pakistan Journal of Pharmaceutical Sciences (Pak. J. Pharm. Sci.) (Vol. 35, No. 6, November 2022, pp. 1595-1601)
DOI: 10.36721/PJPS.2022.35.6.REG.1595-1601.1
Study Site: Liaquat National Hospital & Medical College, Karachi
Ethics Approval: App#0592-2020 LNH-ERC (Liaquat National Hospital Ethical Committee)
Sample Size: N = 134 non-adherent carbapenem prescriptions in Medical ICU/HDU (Dec 2020 - May 2021)
Key Evidence Summary: Prospective interventional study at Liaquat National Hospital evaluating physician acceptance and clinical outcomes of pharmacist-led Antimicrobial Stewardship Program (ASP) interventions for carbapenem therapy. ASP interventions were accepted in 117/134 (87.3%) patients, resulting in 7-day clinical improvement in 99 (84.6%) patients and a significant reduction in 30-day readmission due to re-infection (p = 0.036). Interventions included renal dose adjustment for creatinine clearance (62.7%, n=84) and antibiotic de-escalation (25.4%, n=34).

publications.title: Regional research priorities for medication safety and pharmacovigilance in gulf cooperation council countries: a modified Delphi consensus study
publications.journal: Saudi pharmaceutical journal : SPJ : the official publication of the Saudi Pharmaceutical Society
publications.abstract_snippet: Adverse drug reactions (ADRs) and medication errors remain major global threats to patient safety. Although Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries have advanced medication safety and pharmacovigilance programs, research priorities remain fragmented and lack expert consensus. To establish consensus on medication safety and pharmacovigilance research priorities across GCC countries using a modified Delphi approach. A two-round, web-based modified Delphi study was conducted between November 2024 and September 2025. Experts from Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Oman, Kuwait, Bahrain, and the United Arab Emirates were recruited based on professional experience. publications.title: Secondary data analysis of Adverse Drug Reactions reported by healthcare professionals and patients: interventions to manage ADRs of ACE inhibitors and ARBs
publications.abstract_snippet: Purpose Prescribing cascades occur when an adverse drug reaction (ADR) of a first medication is treated with a second medication, potentially leading to polypharmacy and harm. While various interventions are recommended to prevent harm, it is unknown which are implemented in daily practice. This study aims to assess the interventions implemented for ADRs of angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers (ARB). Methods This cross-sectional study analysed secondary data from spontaneous ADR reports submitted to the Netherlands Pharmacovigilance Center Lareb. Reports were included if the ADR was suspected to be caused by an ACE inhibitor or ARB and an intervention was documented. publications.title: First case report of polymyxin B-induced drug fever in a patient with carbapenem-resistant <i>Acinetobacter baumannii</i> pneumonia
publications.abstract_snippet: The escalating global prevalence of carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacteria has significantly constrained therapeutic options, leading to the revived use of polymyxins. However, this resurgence has been paralleled by an increase in reports of associated adverse effects. No case of drug fever induced by polymyxin B (PMB) has been reported in the literature to date. We report the first case of drug fever (≥39 °C) induced by intravenous PMB in a patient with severe pneumonia caused by carbapenem-resistant  Acinetobacter baumannii , accompanied by tachypnea following concomitant nebulized PMB administration. Upon intervention by the clinical pharmacist, which involved discontinuation of PMB and adjustment of the anti-infective regimen, the patient's fever resolved promptly and the infection was successfully controlled. publications.title: Antimicrobial resistance patterns in a Qatari tertiary care center in 2024: A retrospective study
publications.abstract_snippet: Background Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a critical global health threat. Local, real-time epidemiological data are the cornerstone of effective antimicrobial stewardship. This study aimed to establish a 2024 baseline for AMR patterns at a major tertiary care center in Qatar to directly guide empirical therapy and stewardship interventions. Methods We conducted a retrospective, cross-sectional analysis of 1,656 positive bacterial cultures from blood, urine, and wound samples collected from 1,218 patients between January 1 and December 31, 2024. Antibiotic susceptibility testing was interpreted per European Committee on Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing (EUCAST) 2024 guidelines. Statistical analysis utilized descriptive statistics and Chi-square tests. Cephamycins have been proposed as carbapenem-sparing alternatives because of their relative stability against ESBL-mediated hydrolysis; however, their clinical effectiveness remains uncertain. publications.abstract_snippet: Objective To analyze data from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database to characterize the adverse effects of caplacizumab, including associated adverse events (AEs) and safety signals in real-world clinical practice. and obtain evidence to support the rational use of this drug in the treatment of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP). publications.title: Clinical Pharmacology in China: Seven Decades of Progress in Discipline Development and Education
publications.abstract_snippet: Clinical pharmacology serves as the central discipline supporting rational clinical medication, innovative drug research, and full-lifecycle pharmaceutical supervision. Domestic clinical pharmacology research began in the 1950s, and the field entered a period of rapid development after 1979 across three phases. This study sorts domestic disciplinary milestones and analyzes three key datasets: among the 1949 registered drug clinical trial institutions nationwide, nearly 50% are located in East China; investigational new drug applications surged from 446 (2012) to 3516 (2025); and the Center for Drug Evaluation issued 631 technical guidelines. The National Natural Science Foundation set up an independent clinical pharmacology discipline classification in 2015. The multi-tiered educational system is further elaborated: the transitional 5-year pharmacy (clinical pharmacology direction) track

publications.abstract_snippet: Sexual dysfunction during SSRI/SNRI treatment is common, but persistent sexual dysfunction after discontinuation remains clinically contested and poorly quantified. This structured narrative review and evidence-informed framework-development exercise integrates published and regulatory evidence available to 14 May 2026 on clinical assessment, sexual-domain documentation, differential diagnosis, counseling, risk minimization, and pharmacovigilance reporting. Persistent symptoms may represent a plausible and potentially severe adverse drug reaction when temporality, persistence, phenotype specificity, and assessment of stronger alternative explanations support that interpretation. publications.title: Antimicrobial susceptibility of priority bacterial pathogens from laboratory samples in Timor-Leste: a retrospective analysis of database (2020-2025)
publications.journal: The Lancet regional health. Southeast Asia
publications.abstract_snippet: Background Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major global health threat, with the highest burden in low-income and middle-income countries where diagnostic and surveillance capacity are often limited. Over the past decade, Timor-Leste has made substantial progress in strengthening microbial diagnostics and AMR surveillance capacity. We aimed to describe antimicrobial susceptibility patterns and temporal trends among priority bacterial pathogens in Timor-Leste between 2020 and 2025. Methods We retrospectively analysed antimicrobial susceptibility patterns for WHO priority pathogens isolated from clinical samples processed at the Laboratory of Health, Instituto Nacional de Saúde Pública de Timor-Leste (INSP-TL), between June 2020 and January 2025. email_drafts.subject: Prospective PhD Application Inquiry — Clinical Pharmacy & Outcomes Research (Dr. Shama Abidi, PharmD, MPhil)
email_drafts.body_text:
Dear Prof. Dr. Günther Fink,

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to express my strong interest in pursuing a PhD under your supervision at Swiss Tropical and Public Health Institute (Switzerland).

I recently read your 2023 publication, "Association Between Antimicrobial Stewardship Programs and Antibiotic Use Globally" (DOI: 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2022.53806), and found its focus directly aligned with my clinical research experience.

I hold a Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) and an MPhil in Pharmacy Practice from the University of Karachi, and I currently serve as a Senior Clinical Pharmacist at Liaquat National Hospital and Medical College. My published work includes "Evaluation of carbapenem antimicrobial stewardship program at a tertiary care hospital: A prospective interventional study", as well as prospective cohort studies on ICU carbapenem antimicrobial stewardship (N=134, achieving an 87.3% physician intervention acceptance rate and 62.7% renal CrCl dose adjustments, p=0.036; PJPS 2022), comparative antianginal pharmacotherapy using the Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ-7) and Naranjo ADR scale (N=110; PJPS 2024), and clinical evaluations of AI decision support versus clinical pharmacist interventions (JPPP 2025).

Research Alignment Rationale:
- Direct methodological and clinical overlap on [antibiotic, antimicrobial, clinical, pharmaceutical, stewardship, ward] with Shama Abidi's verified publication "Evaluation of carbapenem antimicrobial stewardship program at a tertiary care hospital: A prospective interventional study" (DOI: 10.36721/PJPS.2022.35.6.REG.1595-1601.1).

I would be very grateful to learn whether your research group anticipates PhD supervision capacity for the upcoming academic intake, and whether university or international doctoral scholarship tracks might be applicable.

I have attached my Curriculum Vitae and published research papers for your review, and I would be honored to discuss a brief PhD research concept note at your convenience.

Thank you very much for your time and consideration.

Warm regards,
Dr. Shama Abidi, PharmD, MPhil (Pharmacy Practice)
Senior Clinical Pharmacist, Liaquat National Hospital & Medical College
